# @local/dsh-desktop-notify
Native Windows system notifications for the DSH agent, with the system sound.
## How it works

- **Host half** (`index.js` + `toast.js`): registers the `notify` tool and sends the
toast directly

through Windows PowerShell + WinRT (`ToastNotificationManager`),
using the DSH AppUserModelID `elect

ron.app.DeepSeek Harness` read from the installed
Start-Menu shortcut, so toasts are branded **DeepS

eek Harness**. Sound is played
explicitly with `System.Media.SoundPlayer` (system WAV), so a muted
n

otification-sound setting does not silence the alert.
- Why not the renderer Web Notification API: o

n the target machine it delivered
nothing at all (not even to the Action Center), while WinRT toasts

do reach the
Action Center. No `node-notifier`/SnoreToast (LGPL) dependency either.

Research note (2026-10-22): DSH exposes no plugin-level notification API (only the
desktop main proc

ess uses Electron `Notification` for mandatory updates), and the
main-process module is not reachabl

e from a plugin. Existing open-source agent
notification tools are CLI hook scripts (macOS `osascrip

t`, PowerShell WinRT, or
`node-notifier` + SnoreToast); none is a DSH plugin. The renderer Web Notif

ication
path is the zero-dependency fit here.
## Tool surface
`notify({ title, body?, sound?, urgency?, tag?, action? })`
| field | meaning |

| `title` | short headline (required) |
| `body` | one or two lines of context |
| `sound` | default

`true`; `false` sends a silent toast |
| `urgency` | `info` (default) / `attention` / `blocked` (bl

ocked uses `requireInteraction`, stays until dismissed) |
| `tag` | a newer toast with the same tag

replaces the older one |
| `action` | `send` (default) or `status` |

Usage guidance given to the model: one notification per meaningful state change —
task finished, blo
cked on the user, or the user asked to be pinged.
## Tests
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Client tests execute the real `client.js` in a Node VM with a mocked
`Notification` class (grant / r

equest-permission / denial paths, silent flag,
round-trip result). Host tests cover the tool schema

(wire-ready JSON Schema),
status, empty-title rejection and a fake-client round-trip.
## Requirements / limitations

- Windows toast permission comes from the DSH desktop app; if Windows notification
settings disable

the app, the tool reports `permission is denied`.
- Desktop-only (needs the DSH desktop renderer and

its Web Notification support).
- Sound volume/focus-assist is controlled by Windows; the plugin can

only choose
silent vs default sound.
详细设计与排障：见 docs/desktop-notify.md。
